mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕旅行与自然人文之美展开，涵盖加拿大的壮丽风光与多元文化（Reading）、野生动物之旅（Extended reading）和与自然和谐同行（Grammar and usage）三个子话题——风光介绍与绿色旅行是高考应用文'邮件/游记/倡议'类的高频场景，旅游与环境亦是雅思经典命题。

subTopics.title: 加拿大：壮丽风光与多元文化
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：Canada is like a blooming flower, unfolding with breathtaking beauty——a land marked with vast lakes and mighty rivers，同时是 ethnically diverse 的国度：languages, cuisine, architecture, art and music will define your encounter。

prompts.task: 你的外国朋友 Chris 计划第一次来中国旅行，向你了解情况。请你用英文回复邮件，内容包括：1. 中国的自然风光；2. 多元的地域文化；3. 表达欢迎并提出帮助。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Chris,

I'm glad to hear that you are planning your first trip to China. Let me tell you what makes my country worth the journey.

China is like a breathtaking artwork painted by Mother Nature: vast land, splendid forests, crystal-clear lakes, mighty rivers and towering mountains all demonstrate its uniqueness and beauty. It is also a nation of distinct regional cultures. Should you find yourself in a local community, languages, cuisine, architecture, art and music will define your encounter — from spicy hotpot streets in the west to quiet water towns in the east.

If you enjoy places off the beaten track, I would be happy to design a route for you. I'm sure China will win your heart with what it has to offer.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: a breathtaking artwork painted by Mother Nature
vast land, splendid forests, crystal-clear lakes

prompts.task: Some people believe that travelling to a country is the best way to learn about its culture. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Many argue that visiting a country in person is the most effective way to understand its culture. I broadly agree, although I would add that travel only educates those who arrive with curiosity and preparation.

The case for travel rests on experience that no screen can reproduce. Culture lives in details — the pace of a street market, the etiquette of a shared meal, the way strangers are greeted — and these are absorbed through the senses rather than described in words. A traveller who orders unfamiliar food, mispronounces greetings and is politely corrected learns more about local values in a week than a reader might in a year. Direct encounters also dismantle stereotypes: people met face to face refuse to stay as simple as the images we brought with us.

Nevertheless, travel is not automatically enlightening. Tourists who move between international hotels and photo spots can circle the globe while meeting nobody, and a short holiday may even harden clichés if visitors see only what brochures promise. Meanwhile, books, films and language study supply the history and context that a two-week trip cannot; without such preparation, much of what a traveller sees remains pretty but meaningless. The deepest understanding therefore comes from combining study beforehand with genuine contact on the ground — ideally staying with local hosts, attempting the language and stepping off the well-worn tourist path.

In conclusion, first-hand experience remains the richest teacher of culture, but only when paired with background knowledge and an open mind. Travel opens the door; the traveller still has to walk through it.

subTopics.title: 野生动物之旅
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：草原 alive with the African wildlife we had come to see——giraffes pulling leaves from the highest branches, elephants with ears flapping lazily，一幅移动的自然长卷。

prompts.task: 暑假里你参加了一次野生动物保护区研学活动。请你为校英文报写一篇英文短文，内容包括：1. 研学见闻；2. 你的收获与感想。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
This summer I joined a study trip to a wildlife reserve in Yunnan, and it turned out to be the most unforgettable lesson of my life.

At dawn, with the sun beating down on the grassland, our tents stood lined up facing the distant mountains. The plains were alive with the wildlife we had come to see: elephants were eating grass, ears flapping lazily as they moved slowly along, while birds rose in noisy clouds above the trees. Watching them, we hardly dared to breathe.

Our guide reminded us that every species here depends on the whole chain of life. When we packed up to leave, no one left a single piece of rubbish behind. Nature offers us her beauty; the least we can do is protect it.

prompts.task: Some people think that too much money is spent on protecting wild animals, and that it should be spent on the human population instead. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Whenever governments fund wildlife conservation, some object that the money would serve people better. I disagree with this view in its strict form, because protecting wild animals and serving human interests are not competing goals but deeply connected ones.

At first glance, the critics seem humane. Hospitals lack beds, schools lack teachers, and millions still live in poverty, so spending fortunes on tigers or rare cranes can look like sentimental luxury. Where budgets are tight, the argument runs, every coin should relieve human suffering first.

This reasoning, however, rests on a false separation between people and nature. Healthy ecosystems purify water, pollinate crops, stabilise the climate and support fisheries on which hundreds of millions depend; when a species disappears, the web that feeds and protects humans weakens with it. Conservation also pays directly: wildlife tourism funds schools and clinics in many rural regions, employing local people as guides and rangers. Moreover, the sums involved are tiny beside military or advertising budgets — the real choice is rarely between saving elephants and building hospitals, but between conservation and far less noble spending.

That said, conservation money must be spent wisely, prioritising whole habitats over headline species and involving local communities rather than fencing them out. Programmes that ignore the people living beside reserves usually fail, and deservedly so.

In conclusion, framing wildlife protection as a theft from human welfare misunderstands both sides of the ledger. A planet that keeps its wild animals is not indulging a hobby; it is maintaining the life-support system on which every human project ultimately depends.

subTopics.title: 与自然和谐同行
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：be in (perfect) harmony with nature、sustainable development、not a bed of roses——把旅行的热情与对自然的尊重放在同一只行囊里。

prompts.task: 暑假将至，请你以学生会名义用英文写一份'绿色出行·文明旅游'倡议书，内容包括：1. 说明背景；2. 提出两三条倡议；3. 发出号召。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear fellow students,

The summer holiday is coming, and many of us are planning trips. However, travelling is not always a bed of roses for nature: rubbish, noise and crowds are hurting the very scenery we love. The Student Union hereby calls on everyone to travel green.

First, respect wildlife — watch animals from a distance instead of feeding them. Second, reduce waste by carrying your own water bottle and taking your rubbish away with you. Third, choose public transport whenever possible.

Travelling in harmony with nature is the only sustainable way to enjoy it. Let's make sure the breathtaking scenery that unfolds before our eyes today will still be there tomorrow!

The Student Union

prompts.task: Tourism brings money to many places, but it can also damage the environment. Do the advantages of tourism outweigh its disadvantages? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
As global travel becomes cheap, tourists pour into beaches, mountains and ancient towns in unprecedented numbers. Whether the benefits of tourism outweigh its environmental costs is hotly debated; my view is that the advantages can outweigh the disadvantages, but only where tourism is deliberately managed.

The economic case for tourism is powerful. It creates jobs for guides, hoteliers and farmers, channels income into regions with few other industries, and gives governments a financial reason to protect scenery and wildlife: a forest that attracts visitors earns more standing than felled. Tourism also funds the maintenance of parks and heritage sites, and exposure to natural beauty builds public support for conservation itself.

The environmental ledger, however, records real damage. Flights and cruise ships emit greenhouse gases; hotels drain water in dry regions; coral reefs are trampled and littered; and quiet ecosystems are disturbed by crowds and construction precisely because they are beautiful. Unmanaged, the industry can consume the very attractions it sells — a process already visible at overcrowded destinations worldwide.

The decisive factor is therefore regulation. Visitor caps, entrance fees reinvested in protection, strict building rules and well-designed trails allow places to profit from tourism while limiting harm; several island nations and national parks already demonstrate that high-value, low-volume tourism works. Where such rules are absent, growth quickly turns destructive.

In conclusion, tourism is neither friend nor enemy of the environment by nature. Managed with discipline, it funds and motivates protection, and its benefits then genuinely outweigh the costs; left to expand freely, it degrades whatever it touches.
